notes.claim_list: Analysis inputs are AnalysisScript_Final.Rmd and Data_Extraction.csv. Supplementary page 9 is S9 in the printed supplement.
notes.sol: Original CSV: https://osf.io/download/5vqd9/?view_only=b9e1e86079c048b4bfb03bee6966e560 . The source explicitly identifies the 131-versus-132 Binary discrepancy and the Figure 2 subgroup-count inconsistencies. Static counts of Task_Output and Task_Type in the original Data_Extraction.csv confirm the references. The paper prints separate Binary counts of 131 in Supplementary Figure S2 and 136 in main Figure 2; both are retained. Its Decide and Categoric counts also disagree with the supplied data. The source changed the human-augmentation Hedges-g denominator before printing pooled estimates; those changed-code estimates are deliberately excluded. The missing secondary moderator input is an additional secondary P0, not a primary-run technical failure.
notes.claude: No paper alternative under R7: four printed counts are wrong (P2). Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: Shipped files verified against the pinned SHA-256 hashes (from the existing scratch download). All counts are direct static row counts of Data_Extraction.csv (370 rows, no missing Task_Type or Task_Output_Cleaned). The shipped script does not filter rows before the bar plots or moderator k_es, so these counts are what the shipped code produces. The supplement's own moderator table (S2.4) prints the shipped-data values (132/180/336/34), which shows that the Figure 2 n column in the main paper (136/184/344; also AI 251 and Human 127 vs 249/121) is inconsistent with the shipped code output. The report states that the Figure 2 plotting code was not shipped. Paper-level 'computational issues' follows from four P2 count discrepancies. 'computationally reproducible' is acceptable because the source report gives that overall verdict and treats these as minor tally inconsistencies; all main estimates reproduce. Side observation: 13 ES_ID values are duplicated in the shipped CSV (357 unique ES_IDs), which would affect the script's printed n_es but not k = 370.
